name: Red Bean Primer (Hồng Đậu Quyết)
concept: The bean-pickers' method, learned on the trellises at the back garden. The student draws Wood or Water qi through the fingertips while sorting red beans, which are bright, pretty and deadly, by touch alone, so that the hand learns which seed is ripe and which is poison before the eye does. It is a gentle method with one hard lesson: a picker who sorts carelessly dies of it. In a fight it sows seeds that ripen into small poisons.
lore: Written by Nghê Hồng Đậu in 912 for the first girls she took in at the manor, two years after she found the sword and planted the beans (C168, A275).

name: Canon of Longing (Tương Tư Kinh)
concept: The manor's own canon, made from a line of an old poem: red beans grow in the southern land, and these most of all are longing. Its poisons do not strike. They ripen. Each Wood stack on a foe grows heavier the longer it is left, as longing does, and the cultivator's charm arts make a foe less willing to break away. Against a careful foe it is slow; against a foe who stays too long it is final.
lore: Nghê Hồng Đậu wrote it between 915 and 960, after she could not open the art of the sword she had found (C168). The manor says she made her own art so as not to need the sword's.
